title: Cuba vs Mexico: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: Choose Cuba if you crave unique cultural immersion, a slower pace, and don't mind a few logistical quirks, budgeting $60-100 USD/day. Opt for Mexico for diverse experiences, culinary adventures, and easier logistics across a wider budget spectrum ($40-150+ USD/day).

categories.name: h2 id="costs-budget">💸 Costs & Budget
categories.summary: Both offer budget options but in very different ways. Cuba is cheaper for local experiences but tricky for modern amenities; Mexico provides a clearer, more versatile budget landscape.

categories.name: h2 id="beaches-coastal-beauty">🏖️ Beaches & Coastal Beauty
categories.summary: Mexico offers a wider variety of accessible, well-equipped beaches for different tastes, from party hubs to serene coves, with better infrastructure for activities and comfort.

categories.name: h2 id="food-drink">🌮 Food & Drink
categories.summary: Mexico's food is incredibly diverse, consistently delicious, and culturally rich, offering options for every palate and budget.

categories.name: h2 id="nightlife-entertainment">💃 Nightlife & Entertainment
categories.summary: Mexico offers a significantly broader and more diverse range of nightlife options, catering to every preference from mega-clubs to sophisticated bars and local cantinas.

categories.name: h2 id="culture-history">🏛️ Culture & History
categories.summary: Cuba offers a truly unique and immersive cultural experience, characterized by its 'frozen-in-time' feel, revolutionary history, and resilient spirit that is unlike anywhere else.

categories.name: h2 id="safety-security">👮 Safety & Security
categories.summary: Cuba offers a significantly lower risk of both violent and petty crime for tourists, providing a more relaxed sense of security.

categories.name: h2 id="getting-there-around">✈️ Getting There & Around
categories.summary: Mexico boasts superior air connectivity, a highly efficient and extensive public transportation network, and easier self-drive options.

categories.name: h2 id="accommodation">🏨 Accommodation
categories.summary: Mexico offers a significantly wider range of accommodation types, styles, and price points, with higher overall quality and easier booking options.

categories.name: h2 id="nature-adventure">⛰️ Nature & Adventure
categories.summary: Mexico offers vastly more diverse natural landscapes and a wider array of adventure activities with better infrastructure and accessibility.

categories.name: h2 id="solo-travel-experience">🚶‍♀️ Solo Travel Experience
categories.summary: Mexico offers superior infrastructure, connectivity, and a thriving social scene that makes meeting other travelers and navigating independently significantly easier for solo adventurers.

faq.question: Is travel to Cuba from the US still restricted?
faq.answer: Yes, direct tourist travel from the US to Cuba is still prohibited. US citizens must travel under one of 12 authorized categories, such as 'support for the Cuban people' or educational activities. However, it's relatively easy to comply with these regulations, often by staying in Casas Particulares and eating at private restaurants.

faq.question: What currency should I use in Cuba and Mexico?
faq.answer: In Cuba, you'll primarily use the Cuban Peso (CUP) for local purchases and Moneda Libremente Convertible (MLC), which is pegged to the USD, for most tourist services. Bring plenty of USD cash as US credit/debit cards generally don't work. In Mexico, the Mexican Peso (MXN) is standard; credit cards are widely accepted, but cash is useful for street vendors and smaller establishments.

faq.question: How reliable is the internet in Cuba vs. Mexico?
faq.answer: Mexico has excellent and widespread internet connectivity, with Wi-Fi readily available in hotels, cafes, and many public spaces, often free. Cuba's internet is limited and generally slow, requiring purchase of ETECSA Wi-Fi cards (about $1 USD/hour) for access at designated hotspots. Expect to be largely offline in Cuba.

faq.question: Which destination is better for families with children?
faq.answer: Mexico is generally better for families due to its wider range of family-friendly resorts, activities (e.g., theme parks, calm beaches with amenities), and reliable infrastructure. Cuba offers a unique cultural experience for older children, but its limited amenities and logistical challenges can be more demanding for families with very young kids.

faq.question: What's the best time of year to visit each country?
faq.answer: For both Cuba and Mexico's Caribbean coast, the dry season from November to April offers the best weather (less humidity, lower chance of hurricanes). May to October is hotter, more humid, and hurricane season. Mexico's Pacific coast and central highlands can be visited year-round, with the rainy season (May-October) often bringing afternoon showers but lush landscapes.

faq.question: Are there good options for vegetarian/vegan travelers?
faq.answer: Mexico is fantastic for vegetarians/vegans, especially in bigger cities and tourist hubs. Many traditional dishes can be made meat-free, and options like tacos de hongos (mushroom tacos) or nopales (cactus) are common. Cuba can be challenging; while rice, beans, and fresh fruit are staples, finding varied meat-free protein sources or dedicated vegetarian restaurants is harder outside of Havana's few specialized paladares.

faq.question: What are the essential packing items for each?
faq.answer: For Cuba: bring all toiletries, medications, and cash you'll need, as supplies can be scarce. A power bank is crucial due to potential outages. For Mexico: sunscreen, insect repellent (especially for jungle areas), a reusable water bottle, and comfortable walking shoes are essential. Both benefit from light, breathable clothing.

faq.question: Can I drink the tap water in Cuba or Mexico?
faq.answer: No, it is generally not safe to drink tap water in either Cuba or Mexico. Always opt for bottled water, purified water, or use a filtered water bottle. Many hotels and Casas Particulares in Cuba will provide purified water for guests, and bottled water is widely available for purchase in both countries.
